headline: Last session: Sensex recovered over 300 points, but Nifty logged its longest weekly losing streak

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 28 September.

why: Indian markets recovered on Friday following heavy midweek losses driven by a sharp sell-off.
Surging crude oil prices above $100 per barrel hit sentiment significantly earlier in the week.
Proposed insurance sector curbs and global market pressures added downside friction on Thursday.
RBI bulletin highlighted economic resilience while noting downside risks from the West Asia conflict.
whatHappening: BSE Sensex ended over 300 points higher in the last session with auto and consumer durables advancing.
NSE Nifty logged its longest weekly losing streak since the Covid-19 market crash in 2020.
The Indian government trimmed FY27 borrowing by ₹1.2 trillion, planning to raise ₹7.8 trillion in H2.
SIDBI withdrew its ₹6,000 crore 3-year bond issuance as market yields hardened.
summary: Indian markets rebounded on Friday with the Sensex rising over 300 points led by auto and consumer durable stocks. Despite the end-of-week recovery, equities ended lower overall for the week due to sharp midweek losses caused by crude oil surges. Consequently, the Nifty recorded its longest weekly losing streak since the 2020 pandemic crash.
